subject: POC trial environment: next steps and success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial environment: next steps and success criteria

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. As discussed, I wanted to capture next steps and propose a concrete POC plan so we can get your team up and evaluating quickly. Attached are the initial evaluation checklist and network requirements we referenced (MVP_Eval_Criteria.xlsx, network_requirements.pdf).

Quick summary / asks:
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for Acme's customer-facing recommendation pipeline (latency, cost, and quality) over a 2-3 week trial.
- Key success criteria (draft) — please confirm or adjust:
  - 95th percentile inference latency <= 150ms for 512-token requests
  - End-to-end throughput to sustain 30 concurrent sessions with <200ms queueing
  - Token-level cost under $0.0009 per token for production-like workload
  - No data leakage: logs retained per your policy; ability to disable retention on request
  - Model outputs meet QA pass rate >= 92% on your validation prompt set (attached)

Environment options (we discussed three):
1) Hosted trial (fastest): Redwood-hosted sandbox using our shared hosted cluster. Pros: minutes to provision, lowest friction. Cons: data stored in Redwood environment; suitable if no strict VPC requirement.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved pool): Dedicated GPU pool for Acme with isolated tenancy. Pros: predictable performance and cost, stronger isolation. Lead time: ~5 business days to allocate and configure.
3) VPC trial (private deployment): Private control plane + VPC peering or on-prem package. Pros: full network isolation and compliance. Lead time: ~2-3 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS setup.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Week 0 (ASAP): Decide environment (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC) and confirm primary success criteria.
- Day 1-2: Provision hosted sandbox (if chosen) or schedule kickoff for dedicated/VPC.
- Day 3-5: Upload sample datasets, share evaluation prompts, configure model choice and quantization settings.
- Week 1-2: Run load/latency tests, collect metrics, iterate on prompt templates and batching config.
- End of Week 2: Review results and determine go/no-go or next phase (pilot).

Owners:
- Redwood: Marissa (POC lead), Aditya (solutions engineer, model + perf tuning), Dev (network & infra lead)
- Acme: Lauren (POC sponsor), Tom (engineering lead)

Please reply with your preferred environment and any tweaks to the success criteria. If you want us to proceed with hosted sandbox to get started immediately, say so and we'll provision and share credentials within one business day.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0189

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. Quick answers from our side:
- We're happy to start with the hosted sandbox to validate performance and quality quickly. If the hosted run meets our criteria, we'll discuss upgrading to a Dedicated sandbox for a longer pilot.
- Success criteria: the latency and QA pass-rate look right; can we relax token-cost to a target of $0.0010/token for the trial? We want to be conservative until we see production tuning results.
- Security: please send the SOC2 summary and an initial network checklist for hosted (we know it's less strict than VPC but need to confirm where logs are stored).

Kickoff availability: our engineering team can kick off on Wednesday (Apr 15). Would you and Aditya be available for a 30-min provisioning + runbook walkthrough at 10:00am PT?

Thanks,
Lauren Miller
Director of ML Engineering, Acme Analytics
lauren@acme-analytics.com

Subject: Re: POC trial environment: next steps and success criteria

Perfect — thanks Lauren. Hosted sandbox it is for initial validation. Responses below and an updated checklist attached (MVP_Eval_Criteria.xlsx) and a short SOW for the POC (redwood-poc-sow.docx).

On cost target: yes — we'll aim for $0.0010/token as the trial target. We'll capture token accounting in the dashboard and annotate cost by route so you can see where optimizations land.

Security/SOC2: I've attached the SOC2 summary in the Drive link (see related links) and included our retention defaults in the checklist. Hosted sandbox defaults to ephemeral logs retained for 30 days; we can disable retention for the trial on a per-route basis if you need that.

Proposed provisioning plan for hosted sandbox (fast path):
- Today (Tue): We create the sandbox project and generate API keys. Dev will publish a short runbook with endpoints and sample curl commands.
- Wed (Apr 15): 10:00am PT — provisioning + runbook walkthrough (30m). Aditya will lead tuning recommendations and baseline perf test commands.
- Wed (Apr 15) EOD: baseline run complete, we'll share initial latency/throughput metrics and a recording of the session.
- Thu-Fri (Apr 16-17): iterative tuning on prompts, batching, and quantization suggestions.

If you opt to switch to Dedicated or VPC after the hosted run, rough timelines: Dedicated ~5 business days; VPC ~2-3 weeks (network approvals + KMS). We'll start network scoping now in parallel if you think VPC will be required later. Dev — please queue the hosted sandbox provisioning and attach the runbook link here when ready.

Action items (owners):
- Marissa: finalize SOW and kick off sandbox provisioning (today).
- Aditya: prepare tuning/runbook and baseline test commands (tomorrow morning).
- Dev: publish network checklist and confirm any IP allowances for the hosted sandbox (tomorrow).
- Lauren/Tom: confirm walkthrough time (10:00am PT Wed) and provide the list of evaluation prompts and validation dataset (if not already shared).

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

—Marissa
